newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks surge on strong Dow, judge's ruling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks surge on strong Dow, judge's ruling.

text.p: Brazilian stocks surged on Monday in heavy trade, boosted by healthy gains on Wall Street and a judge's decision to throw out an injunction aimed at blocking the government's B Band cellular selloff, traders said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most-active stocks closed up 2.75 percent to close at 89,593. Volume was heavy at at 534 million reais ($508.5 million).
Benchmark Telebras preferred shares soared 3.89 percent to close at 104.10, with common shares gaining 2.87 percent at 100.30.

Telebras shares and the market as a whole got a boost from a judge's decision late in the day to throw out an injunction aimed at scuttling the government's plans to offer concessions to operate B Band cellular service to the private sector.
But traders said shares also rode higher on a soaring Dow, which powered up 77 points to 7009 in late afternoon.
"Everything together really helped the market. But I think our gains came mostly from New York," said John Carioba, a trader at Indusval brokerage house in Sao Paulo.
Traders said the market's continued refusal to take profits after weeks of strong gains was beginning to surprise them.

"You feel like the market has got to start taking profits but it never happens it just keeps going up," said one trader, who added that the Bovespa was up well over 20 percent since the beginning of the year.

The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index (IEE) closed up 1.41 percent, rising to 2526 points. The index, which includes the nine most liquid power stocks, was driven upward by gains in state-owned power company Eletrobras. Eletrobras preferred shares rose 2.13 percent to close at 480, on the market's positive mood.
